profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at Natera
profile.summary:
I've been doing web development in one form or another since 1996. I work primarily in node and other flavors of javascript, but can also work in dart/flutter, python, ruby, php, and other languages as needed. Specialties: web application development in multiple languages, software testing, humane design, and technology for sustainable agriculture and farmers markets. I am currently using or am familiar with all the commonly used tools of the trade, and am comfortable up and down the full tech stack.
 
As a senior developer at Infinity Interactive, I have written lab management systems for cutting edge bio-labs, built touchscreen interfaces for lab robots, created data collection tools for blasting crews, provided an interface into years' worth of legal news stories from around the world, fabricated an end-use web application for individuals to organize and file their taxes, designed back-office tools to streamline storage of financial documents, and much more.

positions.title: Owner / Operator
positions.description:
My main product is a complete hosted online farmers market system, written from the ground up using Ruby on Rails and now in use by hundreds of markets and thousands of farmers across North America. When my first version went online in 2002 (then a PHP project), it was the first online farmers market in the world. Since I released the system for use in other communities in 2007, nearly $16,000,000 in direct farmer sales has gone through it. 

This is a one-person operation, so I do everything from design and coding to system administration to customer support.

positions.title: Team Lead / Sr. Software Engineer
positions.description: Part of a team of top shelf hired gun developers, working on a variety of projects for clients world wide. My current specialties on the team include node and ruby development, automated testing and deployment, and quick adaptation to a variety of scripting languages and deployment environments.

positions.title: Head of Testing
positions.description: I joined Partner Software a few months after its founding. Over the course of my career there, as is often the case with software startups, I did pretty much every job a software company has to offer. Of note, I developed an extensive web-based system configuration tool and a workflow management system. Both were built to run internally on networks well behind state of the art. I also built an extensible and configurable data-to-PDF reporting system that took the place of expensive systems like Crystal Reports. The initial version used XSL and Apache's FOP, and the most recent version used java's iText.

positions.title: Engineering Tech
positions.description: Managed the utility's GIS, ran the materials warehouse, did electrical field design work, oversaw the conversion of enterprise software systems.

honors.title: Barbara Petit Pollinator of the Year
honors.description:
From Georgia Organics' Press Release:

Wagoner was honored with the Barbara Petit Pollinator Award for creating LocallyGrown.net, an online local produce marketplace and has become a national model for connecting growers to consumers and building community around local food. The LocallyGrown.net system emulates aspects of traditional farmers markets— customers buy local produce directly from farmers at prices set by the grower—while helping farmers expand their operations online.

Wagoner, a long-time resident of Athens, started LocallyGrown.net there in 2002, and in 2007 it expanded to 10 service areas across the country, including three more in Georgia. Currently, the Locally Grown network has expanded to 116 chapters in Georgia and 526 across the country.

“No other person has facilitated revenues for farmers and connected consumers with local produce quite like Eric Wagoner,” said Georgia Organics Executive Director Alice Rolls.  “He is truly Mr. Farm to Fork.”

Wagoner has connected an incredible amount of consumers with local produce, and the result has been significant revenue for farmers.  Last year, Georgia shoppers bought more than $1.2 million of local produce through locallygrown.net, and nationwide that figure is just shy of $3 million in grower-to-consumer sales.

The Barbara Petit Pollinator Award honors an individual or organization for outstanding community leadership in Georgia’s sustainable farming and food movement. The award acknowledges exceptional success in advancing Georgia Organics’ mission by spreading—pollinating—the movement throughout community life, such as the food industry, faith communities, public agencies, schools, and institutions. The award is named after Barbara Petit, a committed leader, culinary professional, and organizer who served as President of Georgia Organics from 2003-2009.

honors.title: Alec Little Environmental Award
honors.description: The Alec Little Environmental Award was established in 1991 as the first major prize that recognizes individuals and organizations for environmental responsibility in the Athens area. The award is named for the late John A. (Alec) Little, who worked closely with many environmental organizations in Georgia.  Thirty people and 14 groups have received the award since it was first presented in 1992.
honors.issuer: Issued by Eugene P. Odum School of Ecology at the University of Georgia · Apr 2012

projects.title: Conference Registration System
projects.description: Wrote a registration system for the annual Southern Sustainable Agriculture Working Group conference, with over 1200 attendees, multiple tracks of presenters, vendors, academic poster displays, and more. The system is written on Ruby on Rails and handles the needs of the registrants and the conference staff, including sponsor advertisements, offsite adjunct activities, multiple meals, several payment options, and more. The system is fully responsive and uses modern web technologies. The core of the system is designed to be re-used each year while new functionality is written as the needs of the conference grow.
